absent_because.max_decompressed_bytes: no compressed payload is accepted: a record is JSON text, and the raw capture its raw_ref names is never opened
absent_because.max_objects: one record yields exactly one Event
absent_because.max_parse_seconds: no wall-clock bound is enforced: the translator reads no clock. Its passes are linear in the record except section 28's polygon pass, which is quadratic in one geometry's positions and is held to isr_record.MAX_GEOMETRY_POSITIONS (refused geometry-over-cap before it runs); section 20's parse_timeout_seconds is the gateway's isolated-worker timeout, and the conformance suite's parser worker kills a decode that overruns its deadline

max_depth.enforced_at: `Adapter.__init_subclass__`'s wrapper calls `adapter.enforce_depth_bound` on the JSON text or the parsed dict before the translator's `to_cdm` runs
max_depth.source: The record contract states no nesting bound, and section 20's max_xml_depth (64) bounds the gateway's XML decoding, not this JSON record. A record nests eight containers at its deepest typed member (a workflow graph attribute), and the deepest JSON document shipped beside these fixtures is a workflow golden nesting eleven; 96 (`isr_record.MAX_DEPTH`, `isr_record.py`) is eight times that, rounded up to a multiple of 32. This is an IMPLEMENTATION CAP and is NOT the format's normative maximum: the graph attribute `value` and stream `replay_capabilities` are open JSON the contract does not bound.

max_input_bytes.enforced_at: `Adapter.__init_subclass__` wraps each translator's own `to_cdm` with `enforce_input_bound` at class-definition time, so the octets are measured and refused before `isr_record.parse` decodes them
max_input_bytes.source: SC ISR 4559 001 section 20 states max_metadata_bytes = 16777216 ('16 MiB uncompressed per response/record boundary') as a PROJECT OPERATING DEFAULT of the gateway's configuration; it is not the normative maximum of any standard, and the record contract states none. The translator takes the same figure for one record (`MAX_INPUT_BYTES`, `adapters/stanag4559_common.py`), so a record the gateway's default admits is a record it admits. This is an IMPLEMENTATION CAP and is NOT the format's normative maximum.

message_types: SC ISR gateway record (urn:synapsecommand:isr:record:1), family workflow: one workflow record, as its UTF-8 octets or the parsed object, becomes one STATUS_CHANGE Event carrying the record verbatim
capabilities.unknown_fields_basis: the record contract is closed at every level and section 6 rejects unknown keys, so a key it does not define is REFUSED (unknown-key), never carried. Source extension material travels where the contract puts it — typed nodes and attributes of the body's graph, and stream replay_capabilities — and is carried verbatim under payload.record with the rest of the record

limitations.summary: provisional internal profile: the input is the SynapseCommand internal ISR gateway record urn:synapsecommand:isr:record:1 (SC ISR 4559 001 section 6), a contract chosen in this project and not a NATO encoding; no STANAG 4559 or AEDP-17/18/19 wire message is read, no NATO binding package is held, and no NATO wire interoperability is claimed (nato_wire_compatibility_verified: false)

the stateful ISR gateway of the specification (authentication, authorisation, policy, persistence, product transfer, CORBA and SOAP sessions, subscriptions, replay control, workflow mutation) is not part of this distribution; the C17, S18 and W19 wire profiles are UNIMPLEMENTED and no peer was exercised

section 6's transport rules (no byte-order mark, strict UTF-8, no duplicate key, no NaN or infinity, no trailing document, integers within 2**53-1) are enforced on octets or text; a parsed dict has passed through the caller's decoder first, which may already have collapsed a duplicate key
revision.semantic_sha256 and raw_ref.sha256 are copied, never recomputed: section 6 gives digest validation to the gateway, and only their syntax (64 lower-case hex digits) is checked here

security labels are carried verbatim in payload.record and enforce nothing (section 9: every event travels in an authenticated access-controlled gateway envelope); a DECLARED label's scheme is not checked against a policy vocabulary, which no binding package supplies

the metadata graph is held to the record contract's own cardinality only (unique node ids, resolving edges, contiguous occurrences of a repeated attribute, nil without a value); which attributes may repeat is a versioned NATO metadata dictionary's to say, none is held, so a conflicting duplicate of a scalar attribute is not detected (acceptance cases PARSE-009 and PARSE-010)

a record with no source_time is an Event of the gateway's receipt: observed_at is captured_at and payload.time_basis is GATEWAY_RECEIPT (section 9), so a consumer reads time_basis before treating observed_at as a source time
source.source_hash carries raw_ref.sha256 only: the capture representation section 9 asks to record beside it survives at payload.record.raw_ref.representation, because SourceHash is closed

section 28's polygon topology is decided edge by edge and vertex by vertex in exact arithmetic (closed, distinct, non-degenerate, simple rings; no crossing or overlapping edges between rings; interior rings inside their exterior and not inside each other; MultiPolygon parts not inside one another at a vertex); interior connectivity is not decided, and a geometry of more than 2048 positions is refused (geometry-over-cap)

Event.geometry is a workflow record's geometry only when its service is gaoi (section 9: 'workflow GAOI geometry; otherwise null'); the geometry of any other service is validated and carried in payload.record only
native_state is the source's token, verbatim: no transition, tasking, publication or deletion is made, and an Event is never an authorisation or a command (sections 5 and 14)
the whole record is carried verbatim under payload.record and Event.residual is null, the specification's golden form; residual: legacy by the dated ruling of 2026-10-24 (ARCHITECTURE.md section 5)
ingest only: from_cdm is the inherited refusal, and the gateway's outbound commands are separate contracts (section 5), never an Event

every fixture is synthetic: the specification bundle's records, with any footprint moved into CONTRIBUTING.md's Baltic rectangle and the semantic digest recomputed by the bundle's rule; no recorded record is evidence here

the evidence RECORD for this adapter is not IN the distribution: `evidence/` is untracked and unpackaged, CI generates the set on every run, and the release pipeline generates the records for every shipped adapter and attaches them to the GitHub Release of the version it publishes. `evidence.available` is true because every published distribution that carries this adapter has that Release, so its records are retrievable by a third party; it says nothing about what the wheel contains

maturity.basis: L3 PROVENANCE VERIFIED, from evidence that runs today: `python -m synapse_cdm.harness --adapter stanag4559_workflow` reports translate, schema, provenance, lossless (basis: ledger, MAPPINGS declared, no LOST leaf) and golden PASS on every fixture, and tests/test_cdm_stanag4559_workflow_adapter.py reproduces the specification bundle's three expected Events for the workflow family byte for byte. Every fixture is synthetic: the bundle's records, written for SC ISR 4559 001, with any footprint moved into this repository's Baltic rectangle. L4 is NOT declared: the adapter is ingest-only, so the roundtrip check is inapplicable rather than passed, and a rung passed vacuously is not a rung declared. No NATO binding package, wire message or peer is part of this evidence.
